comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C22-C25 regarding initial fitness cost measurements. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with adequate statistical support (Spearman correlations). No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Disagreement on claims C26-C27, C52 regarding fitness recovery patterns. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate Kruskal-Wallis test. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more temporal detail, formal statistical analysis of associations, and explanation of anomalous T60 lines with worse fitness.

Disagreement on claims C3, C16, C28-C31, C34, C55-C56, C63, C71-C74 regarding antibiotic-specific resistance patterns. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate Fisher's Exact tests. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, criticizing 'overly qualitative' presentation and requesting 'synthetic quantitative analysis' and better data visualization rather than categorical descriptions.

Disagreement on claims C32-C33, C75-C76 regarding fitness-resistance correlation. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests (Mann-Whitney U-test, correlation analysis). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting 'more formal statistical analysis' and temporal dynamics data to establish causal link.

Disagreement on claims C35-C37, C57-C58 regarding absence of reversion mutations and presence of compensatory mutations. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED despite limited sample size (15/138 strains). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding mutational analysis 'superficial' and requesting data on mutation timing, functional relationships, and correlation with phenotypic changes.

Disagreement on claims C5, C17, C38, C58 regarding compensatory evolution mechanism. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED based on sequencing and phenotypic data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, challenging whether the evidence supports compensation specifically (point 4: epistasis evidence 'not for compensation per se') and noting lack of functional depth and temporal correlation.

Partial overlap on claims C18-C19, C39, C53 regarding compensatory mutations and their mechanisms. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with functional annotation and experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate the broader compensatory evolution claims UNCERTAIN but do not specifically challenge the marR and envZ experimental findings.

Agreement on claims C41-C42, C45 regarding epistatic effects and context-dependent fitness. Both evaluations find the experimental data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note epistasis alone doesn't demonstrate compensation (point 4) but don't challenge the specific marR* experimental findings on fitness and resistance.

Agreement on claims C43-C44, C46 regarding marR* effects on resistance and membrane permeability. Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and statistical tests. Peer reviewers accept the experimental findings despite questioning broader compensatory evolution interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C77-C80 regarding membrane permeability measurements. Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED with appropriate controls (CCCP) and statistical support (Tukey's post-hoc tests). No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claim C47 regarding envZ mutations showing similar compensatory effects as marR. Both evaluations find claim SUPPORTED with data in supplementary figures. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C69-C70 regarding AUGC fitness metric validation. Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical validation. No concerns raised by either evaluation about the fitness measurement methodology.

Disagreement on claims C64-C65 regarding clinical concordance with tetracycline resistance loss. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by concordance between clinical and laboratory data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'comparison to clinical restriction is problematic' due to ecological factors, lack of geographic isolation, and cross-resistance from continued antibiotic use.

Disagreement on claims C66-C67 regarding clinical concordance with trimethoprim resistance maintenance. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by concordance between clinical and laboratory observations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with same concerns as C64-C65 about problematic clinical comparisons.

Disagreement on claims C6, C68 regarding policy implications and clinical applicability. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED while acknowledging caveats about clinical applicability. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising substantial concerns about clinical comparison validity and study limitations regarding selection regime.

Minimal overlap on claim C63 regarding differential resistance loss patterns. OpenEval finds claim SUPPORTED as part of broader antibiotic-specific patterns (R4). Peer reviewers include C63 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of resistance pattern claims (R3), requesting better quantitative presentation.

Minimal overlap on claim C4 regarding antibiotic-specific resistance loss. OpenEval finds claim SUPPORTED by differential MIC patterns. Peer reviewers include C4 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of clinical implications (R9), questioning the clinical comparison validity.

Disagreement on claims C1-C2, C7-C14, C48-C51, C59-C61 regarding background knowledge and literature review. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as appropriately cited background. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating 'introduction is somewhat lagging' and 'claims in the introduction are not always supported by appropriate citations,' noting inadequate framing and citation support.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about claim C62 regarding mar regulon activity. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental validation of mechanistic claim. Peer reviewers include C62 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of introduction claims, noting inadequate citation support.

OpenEval finds claims C15, C20-C21 regarding experimental system characterization SUPPORTED based on appropriate citation to prior work (Lázár et al., 2014). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
